sourcedFrom: OWNERS MANUAL FOR 500® AND 590® SHOCKWAVE® AND COMPACT CRUISER® PUMP ACTION FIREARMS — Part No. 103855 (Pump Action Firearms), typeset 2/27/18 (2018 (typesetting stamp 2/27/18; no copyright line is printed anywhere in this book))
cleanIntro: This is Mossberg's own procedure for the 590 Shockwave, from the separate Pump Action FIREARMS book — not the shotgun manual. Two things about your gun decide this guide. First, it is a 590: the front of the magazine tube is closed by a MAGAZINE CAP with the magazine spring and its retainer compressed behind it, not by the 500's takedown screw. Second, it wears a Shockwave Technologies RAPTOR GRIP, and the grip comes off before the receiver can be worked on. The Compact Cruiser sections in this same book describe a folding handle and a PISTOL grip — a different product, and none of that wording is carried across here.

steps.title: Safety fully rearward before anything else
steps.action: Push the tang safety button fully to the rear so it reads ON and keep the muzzle in a safe direction. On a Shockwave you are holding the gun at waist level by the forearm strap and the grip, so establish that direction deliberately before you start handling it.
steps.quote: Move the safety button fully rearward to the “ON” (SAFE) position and keep the muzzle pointed in a safe direction while unloading the firearm.
steps.cite: OWNERS MANUAL FOR 500® AND 590® SHOCKWAVE® AND COMPACT CRUISER® PUMP ACTION FIREARMS — Part No. 103855 (Pump Action Firearms), typeset 2/27/18 — UNLOADING — p.10
steps.warn: Upon firing, recoil force will cause the firearm to move rearward and upward. Never hold the firearm at eye level and attempt to sight down the barrel.

steps.title: Take the chambered round out by hand
steps.action: Depress the action lock lever behind the trigger guard and pull the forearm back SLOWLY, far enough that the live shell is withdrawn and lying visible in the ejection port. Lift it out with your fingers rather than cycling it clear.
steps.quote: Depress the action lock lever and pull the forearm rearward, slowly, until the live shotshell is completely withdrawn and visible in the ejection port. Remove shotshell by hand.
steps.cite: OWNERS MANUAL FOR 500® AND 590® SHOCKWAVE® AND COMPACT CRUISER® PUMP ACTION FIREARMS — Part No. 103855 (Pump Action Firearms), typeset 2/27/18 — UNLOADING — p.10

steps.title: Empty the magazine tube through the loading port
steps.action: Turn the firearm so the trigger guard is up, put your thumb into the loading port and press the cartridge stop on the right-hand side. One shell releases per press; keep going until the tube is empty.
steps.quote: Insert your thumb into the opening in the bottom of the receiver and depress the cartridge stop on the right side to release shotshells one at a time (Fig. 9). Repeat until all shotshells are removed from the magazine tube.
steps.cite: OWNERS MANUAL FOR 500® AND 590® SHOCKWAVE® AND COMPACT CRUISER® PUMP ACTION FIREARMS — Part No. 103855 (Pump Action Firearms), typeset 2/27/18 — UNLOADING — p.10

steps.title: Look AND feel — chamber, elevator, magazine tube
steps.action: Open the action fully and check all three places a shell can sit. Mossberg wants a visual and a physical check, so put a finger in as well as an eye.
steps.quote: Depress the action lock lever and pull the forearm completely rearward. Visually and physically inspect chamber, elevator and magazine tube to be certain the firearm is completely unloaded.
steps.cite: OWNERS MANUAL FOR 500® AND 590® SHOCKWAVE® AND COMPACT CRUISER® PUMP ACTION FIREARMS — Part No. 103855 (Pump Action Firearms), typeset 2/27/18 — UNLOADING — p.10
steps.warn: Leave the action in the open, rearward position and the safety button fully rearward in the “ON” (SAFE) position.

steps.title: Re-verify, and put your glasses on
steps.action: Confirm the safety is still fully rearward, re-check chamber, elevator and magazine tube, and put eye protection on. The magazine spring is about to be released and there is oil in the receiver tracks.
steps.quote: Move the safety button fully rearward to the “ON” (SAFE) position and visually and physically check the chamber, elevator, and magazine tube to be certain the firearm is unloaded before disassembling the firearm. Wear eye protection during disassembly and cleaning to protect your eyes from oil splatter or spring loaded components.
steps.cite: OWNERS MANUAL FOR 500® AND 590® SHOCKWAVE® AND COMPACT CRUISER® PUMP ACTION FIREARMS — Part No. 103855 (Pump Action Firearms), typeset 2/27/18 — DISASSEMBLY — p.10

steps.title: Park the bolt mid-port
steps.action: Depress the action lock lever and run the forearm all the way back, then ease it forward until the front face of the bolt sits in the MIDDLE of the ejection port. That is the position the rest of the strip assumes.
steps.quote: Depress the action lock lever and open the action by sliding the forearm fully rearward. Move the forearm slowly forward from the fully rearward position until the front of the bolt is in the middle of the ejection port.
steps.cite: OWNERS MANUAL FOR 500® AND 590® SHOCKWAVE® AND COMPACT CRUISER® PUMP ACTION FIREARMS — Part No. 103855 (Pump Action Firearms), typeset 2/27/18 — DISASSEMBLY — p.10

steps.title: Magazine cap off — under spring pressure
steps.action: Unscrew the magazine cap at the front of the tube, counterclockwise. Cup a hand over the end as it releases: the magazine spring retainer and the magazine spring are behind it and they are compressed.
steps.prose: This is the 590 branch of the book. The 500 Shockwave on the facing instruction uses a takedown screw with nothing sprung behind it — that is a different gun on the same page.
steps.quote: Unscrew the magazine cap by turning it counterclockwise (Fig. 10).
steps.cite: OWNERS MANUAL FOR 500® AND 590® SHOCKWAVE® AND COMPACT CRUISER® PUMP ACTION FIREARMS — Part No. 103855 (Pump Action Firearms), typeset 2/27/18 — DISASSEMBLY, “590® Models:” — p.11
steps.warn: The 590® Model magazine spring retainers and springs are under significant spring pressure. Use caution to prevent injury to yourself or others around you.

steps.title: Twist the barrel out
steps.action: Draw the barrel forward off the magazine tube and out of the receiver, rocking it gently back and forth as it comes. Do not lever on it.
steps.quote: Remove the barrel from the receiver with a gentle back-and-forth rotational movement while pulling the barrel out of the receiver assembly.
steps.cite: OWNERS MANUAL FOR 500® AND 590® SHOCKWAVE® AND COMPACT CRUISER® PUMP ACTION FIREARMS — Part No. 103855 (Pump Action Firearms), typeset 2/27/18 — DISASSEMBLY — p.11

steps.title: Raptor Grip off the receiver
steps.action: Take the plug out of the rear of the Raptor Grip with a slotted screwdriver, then slacken the socket head cap screw underneath it with a 1/4 inch Allen wrench. Pull the grip off the back of the receiver.
steps.prose: The grip is a single bolt into the rear of the receiver, behind a cosmetic plug. Nothing else comes off with it, and the plug is small enough to lose — put it with the screw.
steps.aside: The PISTOL GRIP REMOVAL procedure on p.11 belongs to the Compact Cruiser, which has a folding handle and a pistol grip. It is not this firearm's grip.
steps.quote: Using a slotted screwdriver, remove the plug from the rear of the Raptor Grip as seen in Figure 13. Using a 1/4” allen head wrench, loosen the socket head cap screw from the Raptor Grip as seen in Figure 14. Pull the Raptor Grip off the receiver as seen in Figure 15.
steps.cite: OWNERS MANUAL FOR 500® AND 590® SHOCKWAVE® AND COMPACT CRUISER® PUMP ACTION FIREARMS — Part No. 103855 (Pump Action Firearms), typeset 2/27/18 — RAPTOR GRIP REMOVAL — p.12

steps.title: Drift the trigger housing pin and lift the housing out
steps.action: Lay the firearm trigger-guard-up on a clean surface. Push out the small-diameter trigger housing retainer pin in the side of the receiver, about half an inch below the rear of the trigger guard, with a punch no larger than 3/16 inch. Lift the REAR of the trigger housing first and take it out.
steps.caution: The trigger housing assembly is a complex assembly and must not be disassembled. Disassembly should only be performed at an authorized Product Service Center or by a qualified gunsmith.
steps.quote: With a punch (no greater than 3/16” [4.76 mm] diameter), push out the small diameter trigger housing retainer pin located on the side of the receiver, approximately a 1/2” (12.7 mm) below the rear of the trigger guard (Fig. 16). Remove the trigger housing assembly by lifting the rear portion upward first.
steps.cite: OWNERS MANUAL FOR 500® AND 590® SHOCKWAVE® AND COMPACT CRUISER® PUMP ACTION FIREARMS — Part No. 103855 (Pump Action Firearms), typeset 2/27/18 — TRIGGER HOUSING ASSEMBLY REMOVAL — p.13
steps.warn: Do not pull the trigger and allow the hammer to fall when the trigger housing assembly is removed from the receiver. To do so may result in personal injury and/or damage to the assembly.

steps.title: Look before you go further
steps.action: Study how the bolt, bolt slide and action slide bar assembly are arranged before you break that arrangement. They go back exactly as they came out and nothing indexes it for you.
steps.quote: Pay special attention to the position of the bolt, bolt slide and action slide bar assembly during this portion of the disassembly, as the parts must be in the same relationship during reassembly.
steps.cite: OWNERS MANUAL FOR 500® AND 590® SHOCKWAVE® AND COMPACT CRUISER® PUMP ACTION FIREARMS — Part No. 103855 (Pump Action Firearms), typeset 2/27/18 — DISASSEMBLY OF INTERNAL RECEIVER COMPONENTS, CAUTION — p.13

steps.title: Cartridge interrupter and cartridge stop out
steps.action: Lift the cartridge interrupter and cartridge stop out of the receiver walls; tap the sides of the receiver lightly if they do not release by hand. Note which wall each came from.
steps.quote: Remove the cartridge interrupter and cartridge stop from the receiver. (It may be necessary to tap the sides of the receiver lightly to release these parts) (Fig. 17).
steps.cite: OWNERS MANUAL FOR 500® AND 590® SHOCKWAVE® AND COMPACT CRUISER® PUMP ACTION FIREARMS — Part No. 103855 (Pump Action Firearms), typeset 2/27/18 — DISASSEMBLY OF INTERNAL RECEIVER COMPONENTS — p.13

steps.title: Lift the bolt slide out at the clearance cuts
steps.action: Run the forearm and action slide assembly back until the bolt and bolt slide are three quarters rearward. When the bottom of the bolt slide lines up with the clearance cuts in the receiver sides, lift it straight up and out.
steps.quote: Move the forearm/action slide assembly rearward so that the bolt assembly and bolt slide are three quarters of the way rearward. When the bottom of the bolt slide is aligned with the clearance cuts in the sides of the receiver, lift the bolt slide upward and out of the receiver (Fig. 18).
steps.cite: OWNERS MANUAL FOR 500® AND 590® SHOCKWAVE® AND COMPACT CRUISER® PUMP ACTION FIREARMS — Part No. 103855 (Pump Action Firearms), typeset 2/27/18 — DISASSEMBLY OF INTERNAL RECEIVER COMPONENTS — p.14

steps.title: Bolt forward and out, then the elevator
steps.action: Slide the bolt assembly FORWARD out through the barrel opening at the front of the receiver. Then pivot the front of the elevator up and squeeze its two arms together to disengage them.
steps.caution: The safety button must be fully rearward in the “ON” (SAFE) position to remove the elevator assembly.
steps.quote: Remove the bolt assembly by sliding it forward and out of the receiver assembly through the barrel opening at the front of the receiver (Fig. 19-A).
steps.cite: OWNERS MANUAL FOR 500® AND 590® SHOCKWAVE® AND COMPACT CRUISER® PUMP ACTION FIREARMS — Part No. 103855 (Pump Action Firearms), typeset 2/27/18 — DISASSEMBLY OF INTERNAL RECEIVER COMPONENTS — p.14

steps.title: Forearm off the magazine tube — field strip complete
steps.action: Slide the forearm and action slide assembly forward off the magazine tube. That is everything the manual sanctions: barrel, forearm/slide, bolt, bolt slide, elevator, cartridge stop, cartridge interrupter, trigger housing, Raptor Grip, and the cap, retainer and spring off the tube.
steps.caution: Field disassembly is now complete! The firearm should not be disassembled further for routine cleaning or maintenance. Further disassembly should only be performed by an Authorized Product Service Center or by a qualified gunsmith.
steps.quote: Remove the forearm/action slide assembly by sliding it forward and off the magazine tube.
steps.cite: OWNERS MANUAL FOR 500® AND 590® SHOCKWAVE® AND COMPACT CRUISER® PUMP ACTION FIREARMS — Part No. 103855 (Pump Action Firearms), typeset 2/27/18 — DISASSEMBLY OF INTERNAL RECEIVER COMPONENTS — p.14

steps.title: Bore and chamber
steps.action: Scrub the bore and chamber with solvent, patch until clean, then a single lightly oiled patch for protection. The Shockwave's barrel is short — check it end to end for anything left in it.
steps.quote: Scrub bore and chamber with solvent and follow with cleaning patches until barrel is clean. A final pass with a lightly oiled patch will provide a protective coating. A stiff brass bristle brush is useful for removing stubborn deposits.
steps.cite: OWNERS MANUAL FOR 500® AND 590® SHOCKWAVE® AND COMPACT CRUISER® PUMP ACTION FIREARMS — Part No. 103855 (Pump Action Firearms), typeset 2/27/18 — BARREL CLEANING — p.15
steps.warn: Be sure not to leave cleaning patches or excessive oil or grease in the bore as they can create dangerous obstructions.

steps.title: Action parts, dry and sparing
steps.action: Clean the bolt, bolt slide and action slide bars with an EVAPORATING solvent, then lubricate sparingly.
steps.quote: Clean all components of the action including the bolt, bolt slide and action slide bars to remove accumulated residue. An evaporating solvent should be used. Action parts will remain cleaner longer if lubrication is used sparingly.
steps.cite: OWNERS MANUAL FOR 500® AND 590® SHOCKWAVE® AND COMPACT CRUISER® PUMP ACTION FIREARMS — Part No. 103855 (Pump Action Firearms), typeset 2/27/18 — ACTION CLEANING — p.15

steps.title: Receiver interior, and the bolt tracks
steps.action: Rag or soft brush inside the receiver, concentrating on the tracks that guide the bolt and bolt slide, then a few drops of light oil in those tracks.
steps.quote: Clean the inside of receiver with a rag or soft brush, giving special attention to the tracks which guide the bolt and bolt slide. Place a few drops of light oil in these tracks when clean. Care should be taken when cleaning the exterior surfaces of the receiver to prevent cosmetic damage. Never use a brush with metal bristles, as this could remove the protective coating on the receiver.
steps.cite: OWNERS MANUAL FOR 500® AND 590® SHOCKWAVE® AND COMPACT CRUISER® PUMP ACTION FIREARMS — Part No. 103855 (Pump Action Firearms), typeset 2/27/18 — RECEIVER CLEANING — p.15

steps.title: Trigger housing — brush only
steps.action: Brush loose residue off the trigger housing with a SOFT bristle brush and leave it assembled.
steps.quote: Brush loose residue from trigger housing with a soft bristle brush. Never use a brush with metal bristles, as this could remove the protective coating on the trigger housing.
steps.cite: OWNERS MANUAL FOR 500® AND 590® SHOCKWAVE® AND COMPACT CRUISER® PUMP ACTION FIREARMS — Part No. 103855 (Pump Action Firearms), typeset 2/27/18 — TRIGGER HOUSING CLEANING — p.16

steps.title: Put the Raptor Grip back — and only the Raptor Grip
steps.action: Refit the Shockwave Technologies Raptor Grip, tighten its socket head cap screw and replace the plug. Do not substitute a buttstock or another pistol grip while it is apart: on this firearm that is a legal change, not a cosmetic one.
steps.prose: Mossberg puts this in capitals in the Shockwave section because the gun's ATF classification depends on the grip it left the factory with.
steps.quote: THIS FIREARM, AS DELIVERED FROM THE FACTORY, IS EQUIPPED WITH A SHOCKWAVE TECHNOLOGIES RAPTOR GRIP ONLY. REPLACING THE SHOCKWAVE TECHNOLOGIES RAPTOR GRIP WITH A BUTTSTOCK OR OTHER PISTOL GRIP MAY CHANGE THIS FIREARM’S ATF CLASSIFICATION, AND MAY RESULT IN A VIOLATION OF NFA REGULATIONS UNLESS THE PROPER ATF FORMS ARE COMPLETED, AND THE TAX IS PAID.
steps.cite: OWNERS MANUAL FOR 500® AND 590® SHOCKWAVE® AND COMPACT CRUISER® PUMP ACTION FIREARMS — Part No. 103855 (Pump Action Firearms), typeset 2/27/18 — 500® AND 590® SHOCKWAVE® — p.22
steps.warn: Also, check with your local licensed retailer or state police for additional restrictions that may be imposed by state or local law or regulation on firearms of this type.

deepAbsentReason: Mossberg publishes nothing deeper than this field strip for the 590 Shockwave and bars going further outside a service centre: “Field disassembly is now complete! The firearm should not be disassembled further for routine cleaning or maintenance. Further disassembly should only be performed by an Authorized Product Service Center or by a qualified gunsmith.” (DISASSEMBLY OF INTERNAL RECEIVER COMPONENTS, p.14). The trigger housing carries its own separate bar on p.13. A deep-clean branch here would have to be invented, so there is none.

cleaning.name: Barrel and magazine tube
tasks: Scrub bore and chamber with solvent; a stiff brass bristle brush shifts stubborn deposits.
Patch until clean, then one lightly oiled patch for a protective coating.
Wipe out the magazine tube while the spring and retainer are out of it.
Confirm the bore is clear of patches, oil and grease before the barrel goes back on.

cleaning.name: Magazine spring group
tasks: Wipe the magazine spring and the spring retainer; check the spring is not kinked or set.
Keep the retainer with the cap — the cap will not seat correctly without it.

cleaning.name: Action group
tasks: Bolt, bolt slide and action slide bars de-residued with an evaporating solvent.
Avoid over-lubrication below freezing; lubricants thicken and can affect operation.

cleaning.name: Receiver
tasks: Rag or soft brush inside; concentrate on the bolt and bolt-slide tracks.
A few drops of light oil in the tracks once clean.
Never a metal-bristle brush on the receiver or the trigger housing.

cleaning.name: Raptor Grip and strap
tasks: Wipe the grip and the rear face of the receiver where it seats.
Check the forearm's fabric strap for wear and that its stitching is sound — you grip through it when firing.
Refit the grip screw and the plug; do not fit any other grip or a buttstock.

cleaning.name: Interval and storage
tasks: Mossberg recommends a thorough clean every 200 rounds, sooner in dust, dirt or harsh weather.
Clean as soon as possible after use, especially after exposure to moisture.
For long storage: thoroughly clean and oil; do not plug the barrel or store in a fabric-lined case that will absorb the lubricant.

reassembly: Receiver trigger-housing opening upward on a clean surface, safety button fully rearward in the ON (SAFE) position.
Forearm assembly onto the magazine tube, guiding the action slide bars into their cuts in the front of the receiver.
Elevator in by squeezing its arms so the studs enter the 1/4 in. holes in the receiver; pivot it level with the outside edge of the cavity.
Bolt assembly in through the barrel opening, bolt lock downward and forward; depress the ejector so the bolt runs fully rearward and seats in its slot in the bolt.
Action slide bars set so the notch lines up with the cuts in the inside receiver walls; elevator pushed down onto the bolt.
Bolt slide in slotted-side up with the notch to the rear, front end lowered first.
Cartridge stop and cartridge interrupter back on their own walls, hooks facing inward toward the centre of the cavity.
Hammer must be fully cocked before the trigger housing will go in. Front lugs into their slots first, then ease the rear down. DO NOT FORCE.
Trigger housing pin pushed in until flush with the side of the receiver.
Barrel in, magazine spring and retainer back in the tube, magazine cap on FINGER TIGHT ONLY.
Raptor Grip back on the rear of the receiver, socket head cap screw tightened with the 1/4 in. Allen wrench, plug replaced.
Confirm the barrel is fully seated by looking through the ejection port before the function test.
fncheck: Muzzle in a safe direction and the firearm proven empty. Depress and hold the action lock lever and open and close the action several times, checking for free movement. Close the action with the safety ON and pull the trigger fully — the hammer should NOT fall. Take your finger off, move the safety to OFF — the hammer should NOT fall. Leave it OFF and pull the trigger — the hammer should fall. Open the action and return the safety to ON. If the firearm does not perform as described at any step, contact the factory authorized Product Service Center immediately and do not attempt to use it.
